# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-cli-reference.py from `rupu --help`; do not edit by hand. -->

Every `rupu` command, argument and flag, generated from the binary's own help.
Narrative guides live in [using-rupu.md](using-rupu.md) and the other docs.

## Global options

These apply to every command.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--format <FORMAT>` | Structured output format for commands that support tabular/report views [possible values: table, pretty, json, jsonl, csv] |
| `--absolute` | Show absolute ISO timestamps in tables instead of relative ages. Useful when correlating a run against external logs |
| `--all-columns` | Keep every table column, including ones that are empty for every row shown. Columns are otherwise suppressed based on the rows actually displayed, so a filtered listing may show fewer columns |
| `--max-open-files <N>` | Raise this process's open-file limit (RLIMIT_NOFILE) to N and cap automatic growth there. Overrides `RUPU_MAX_OPEN_FILES` and `[runtime].max_open_files`. Wide fan-outs hold several descriptors per concurrent agent |

<a id="rupu-run"></a>
### `rupu run`

One-shot agent run, or pause/resume a run by id

```
rupu run [OPTIONS]
```

<a id="rupu-run-agent"></a>
### `rupu run <agent>`

Run one agent, optionally against a repo/PR/issue target

```
rupu run [OPTIONS] <AGENT> [TARGET] [PROMPT]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<AGENT>` | Agent name (matches an `agents/*.md` file) |
| `[TARGET]` | Optional target reference, e.g. `github:owner/repo#42`. See `docs/scm.md#target-syntax` for the full grammar. Distinguished from `prompt` by parsing as a RunTarget |
| `[PROMPT]` | Optional initial user message. Defaults to "go" if omitted |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--prompt <PROMPT_FLAG>` | Explicit prompt flag (takes precedence over the positional `prompt`). Use this when the prompt should not be confused with a target string |
| `--mode <MODE>` | Override permission mode (`ask` \| `bypass` \| `readonly`) |
| `--no-stream` | Don't render tokens as they arrive; show each response once it is complete. The request still streams on the wire, so long responses can't hit the request timeout |
| `--view <VIEW>` | Control live output density (`focused` \| `full`) [possible values: focused, compact, full] |
| `--into <PATH>` | For `<platform>:<owner>/<repo>` targets: clone into this directory instead of the default `./<repo>/`. The directory must not already exist (refuse-by-default — pass an explicit path you own). Mutually exclusive with `--tmp` |
| `--tmp` | For `<platform>:<owner>/<repo>` targets: clone into a temporary directory that is auto-deleted on exit. Useful for one-shot agents that produce findings without modifying the repo. Mutually exclusive with `--into` |
| `--run-id <RUN_ID>` | Pre-assign the run id (so a caller can reference the run before it starts) |
| `--findings-profile <PROFILE>` | Findings contract for this run (`full` \| `summary`), overriding the agent's `findingsProfile`. A placed workflow unit's coordinator passes its step's resolved profile this way |
| `--engagement-profile <ID>` | Engagement profile(s) for this run — the asset domain(s) findings are validated against (e.g. `network`, `binary`, or a composite like `pentest`). Repeatable or comma-separated. Empty = the `code` path [aliases: --engagement-profiles] |
| `--continue <AGENT_RUN_ID>` | Continue an interrupted run of this agent from its transcript instead of starting fresh: the earlier conversation is rebuilt and the agent is told it was interrupted. A run that had already finished prints its recorded answer without calling the model. Run it from the same project as the original run. With `--model` or `--provider`, a run that failed on a provider-side outcome (a refusal, say) is continued too, on that model |
| `--model <MODEL>` | Model for this run, overriding the agent's `model:` and the config default |
| `--provider <PROVIDER>` | Provider for this run, overriding the agent's `provider:` and the config default |

<a id="rupu-run-pause"></a>
### `rupu run pause`

Pause a running workflow run by id

```
rupu run pause <RUN_ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<RUN_ID>` | Full run id (`run_<ULID>`) as printed by `rupu run` / `rupu workflow run` |

<a id="rupu-run-resume"></a>
### `rupu run resume`

Resume a paused workflow run by id

```
rupu run resume [OPTIONS] <RUN_ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<RUN_ID>` | Full run id (`run_<ULID>`) of the run to resume |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--mode <MODE>` | Override permission mode for the resumed run (`ask` \| `bypass` \| `readonly`) |
| `--plain` | Use the plain line printer instead of the live graph view |
| `--restart-interrupted` | Start every interrupted step and `for_each` unit over from its prompt instead of continuing it from its transcript |

<a id="rupu-run-list"></a>
### `rupu run list`

List recent workflow runs, newest first

```
rupu run list [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--limit <LIMIT>` | Return at most N runs, newest first [default: 10000] |
| `--status <STATUS>` | Filter by status (`running`, `completed`, `failed`, …) |

<a id="rupu-run-show"></a>
### `rupu run show`

Show one workflow run's detail

```
rupu run show <RUN_ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<RUN_ID>` | Full run id (`run_<ULID>`) |

<a id="rupu-agent"></a>
### `rupu agent`

Manage agents

```
rupu agent [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Description |
|---|---|
| [`list`](#rupu-agent-list) | List all available agents (global + project) |
| [`show`](#rupu-agent-show) | Print an agent's frontmatter and body |
| [`edit`](#rupu-agent-edit) | Open an agent file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR`. Validates the frontmatter on save (warn-only) |
| [`validate`](#rupu-agent-validate) | Check agent files: each must parse and its `tools:` must name known tools (an unknown name is a load error). Checks every file in the global and project agent dirs with `--all`, shadowed ones included. Exits nonzero when any check fails |
| [`create`](#rupu-agent-create) | Scaffold a new agent file, then open it for editing. Prompts interactively for scope and name when omitted. With `--describe`, a model drafts the definition before you review it |

<a id="rupu-agent-list"></a>
### `rupu agent list`

List all available agents (global + project)

```
rupu agent list [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output (also honored: `NO_COLOR` env, `[ui].color = "never"` in config) |

<a id="rupu-agent-show"></a>
### `rupu agent show`

Print an agent's frontmatter and body

```
rupu agent show [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` | Name of the agent |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output (also honored: `NO_COLOR` env var) |
| `--theme <THEME>` | syntect theme name. Default: `base16-ocean.dark` |
| `--pager` | Force pager. Default: page when stdout is a tty |
| `--no-pager` | Disable pager |

<a id="rupu-agent-edit"></a>
### `rupu agent edit`

Open an agent file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR`. Validates the frontmatter on save (warn-only)

```
rupu agent edit [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` | Name of the agent |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--scope <SCOPE>` | Force the project shadow (`.rupu/agents/<name>.md`) or the global file (`<global>/agents/<name>.md`). Default: prefer project if it exists, else global [possible values: global, project] |
| `--editor <EDITOR>` | Override the editor (e.g. `--editor "code --wait"`). Default: `$VISUAL` then `$EDITOR` then `vi` |

<a id="rupu-agent-validate"></a>
### `rupu agent validate`

Check agent files: each must parse and its `tools:` must name known tools (an unknown name is a load error). Checks every file in the global and project agent dirs with `--all`, shadowed ones included. Exits nonzero when any check fails

```
rupu agent validate [OPTIONS] <NAME|--all>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `[NAME]` | Name of the agent (frontmatter `name:` or file stem) |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--all` | Check every agent file in both layers |

<a id="rupu-agent-create"></a>
### `rupu agent create`

Scaffold a new agent file, then open it for editing. Prompts interactively for scope and name when omitted. With `--describe`, a model drafts the definition before you review it

```
rupu agent create [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `[NAME]` | Name for the new agent (no `.md` extension) |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--scope <SCOPE>` | Target scope (`global` or `project`). Prompts when omitted [possible values: global, project] |
| `--editor <EDITOR>` | Override the editor (e.g. `--editor "code --wait"`) |
| `--describe <DESCRIBE>` | Natural-language description — a model drafts the agent |
| `--gen-provider <GEN_PROVIDER>` | Provider for generation (default: first authenticated) |
| `--gen-model <GEN_MODEL>` | Model for generation (default: provider's default) |
| `--host <HOST>` | Host to create on (only `local` available today) [default: local] |

<a id="rupu-workflow"></a>
### `rupu workflow`

Manage workflows

```
rupu workflow [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Description |
|---|---|
| [`list`](#rupu-workflow-list) | List all workflows (global + project) |
| [`show`](#rupu-workflow-show) | Inspect a workflow definition |
| [`edit`](#rupu-workflow-edit) | Open a workflow file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR`. Validates the YAML on save (warn-only) |
| [`create`](#rupu-workflow-create) | Scaffold a new workflow YAML from a template, then open it for editing. Prompts interactively for scope and name when omitted. With `--describe`, a model drafts the definition before you review it |
| [`run`](#rupu-workflow-run) | Run a workflow |
| [`runs`](#rupu-workflow-runs) | List recent workflow runs from the persistent run-store (`<global>/runs/`). Newest first |
| [`show-run`](#rupu-workflow-show-run) | Inspect one persisted run: status, inputs, per-step transcript pointers |
| [`approve`](#rupu-workflow-approve) | Approve a paused run and resume execution from the awaited step. The run must be in `awaiting_approval` status |
| [`reject`](#rupu-workflow-reject) | Reject a paused run. Marks it `rejected`; no further steps dispatch |
| [`cancel`](#rupu-workflow-cancel) | Cancel a running workflow run |
| [`pause`](#rupu-workflow-pause) | Cooperatively pause a running workflow run at its next safe boundary, leaving it non-terminal and resumable via `rupu workflow resume` |
| [`resume`](#rupu-workflow-resume) | Resume a failed/cancelled run, re-running only the agent runs that didn't succeed. An agent run the interrupted process left mid-flight is picked up where it stopped (or its finished answer reused) rather than started over |
| [`archive-run`](#rupu-workflow-archive-run) | Archive a terminal run (move it out of the active list; reversible) |
| [`restore-run`](#rupu-workflow-restore-run) | Restore an archived run back to the active list |
| [`delete-run`](#rupu-workflow-delete-run) | Permanently delete a run and its transcripts. Requires `--force` |

### `rupu workflow edit`

<a id="rupu-workflow-create"></a>
### `rupu workflow create`

Scaffold a new workflow YAML from a template, then open it for editing. Prompts interactively for scope and name when omitted. With `--describe`, a model drafts the definition before you review it

```
rupu workflow create [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `[NAME]` | Workflow name (no `.yaml` extension) |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--scope <SCOPE>` | Target scope (`global` or `project`). Prompts when omitted [possible values: global, project] |
| `--editor <EDITOR>` | Override the editor (e.g. `--editor "code --wait"`) |
| `--describe <DESCRIBE>` | Natural-language description — a model drafts the workflow |
| `--gen-provider <GEN_PROVIDER>` | Provider for generation (default: first authenticated) |
| `--gen-model <GEN_MODEL>` | Model for generation (default: provider's default) |
| `--host <HOST>` | Host to create on (only `local` available today) [default: local] |

<a id="rupu-workflow-run"></a>
### `rupu workflow run`

Run a workflow

```
rupu workflow run [OPTIONS] [NAME] [TARGET]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `[NAME]` | Workflow name (filename stem under `workflows/`). Omit when running from a file with `--file` |
| `[TARGET]` | Optional run-target: a repo, PR, or issue reference. Accepts repo (`github:owner/repo`, `gitlab:group/proj`), PR (`github:owner/repo#42`), or issue (`github:owner/repo/issues/42`). Repo / PR targets clone to a tmpdir for the run; issue targets pre-fetch the issue payload and bind it as `{{ issue.* }}` in step prompts. |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--input <INPUT>` | `KEY=VALUE` template inputs (repeatable) |
| `--mode <MODE>` | Override permission mode (`ask` \| `bypass` \| `readonly`) |
| `--view <VIEW>` | Control live output density (`focused` \| `full`) [possible values: focused, compact, full] |
| `--plain` | Use the plain line printer instead of the live graph view |
| `--run-id <RUN_ID>` | Pre-assign the run id (e.g. so a caller can reference the run before it starts) |
| `--engagement-profile <ID>` | Engagement profile(s) for this run — the asset domain(s) every step's findings are validated against (e.g. `network`, `binary`, or a composite like `pentest`). Repeatable or comma-separated. Empty = the `code` path [aliases: --engagement-profiles] |
| `--file <PATH>` | Run a workflow directly from a file path instead of resolving a name from the catalog. The workflow is not added to the catalog |

<a id="rupu-workflow-runs"></a>
### `rupu workflow runs`

List recent workflow runs from the persistent run-store (`<global>/runs/`). Newest first

```
rupu workflow runs [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--limit <LIMIT>` | Show only the N most recent runs [default: 50] |
| `--status <STATUS>` | Filter by status: `pending` / `running` / `completed` / `failed` / `awaiting_approval` / `rejected` |
| `--issue <ISSUE>` | Filter by issue ref (full or shorthand). Matches the textual `RunRecord.issue_ref` persisted at run start. Accepts `<platform>:<owner>/<repo>/issues/<N>` (full), `<owner>/<repo>#<N>` (GitHub shorthand), or bare `<N>` (autodetects from cwd's git remote) |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output (also honored: `NO_COLOR` env, `[ui].color = "never"` in config) |

<a id="rupu-workflow-show-run"></a>
### `rupu workflow show-run`

Inspect one persisted run: status, inputs, per-step transcript pointers

```
rupu workflow show-run [OPTIONS] <RUN_ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<RUN_ID>` | Full run id (`run_<ULID>`) as printed by `rupu workflow run` |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--view <VIEW>` | Live view density for the retained snapshot [possible values: focused, compact, full] |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output (also honored: `NO_COLOR` env, `[ui].color = \"never\"` in config) |
| `--pager` | Force pager. Default: page when stdout is a tty |
| `--no-pager` | Disable pager |

<a id="rupu-workflow-approve"></a>
### `rupu workflow approve`

Approve a paused run and resume execution from the awaited step. The run must be in `awaiting_approval` status

```
rupu workflow approve [OPTIONS] <RUN_ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<RUN_ID>` | Full run id (`run_<ULID>`) of the run awaiting approval |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--mode <MODE>` | Override permission mode for the resumed run (`ask` \| `bypass` \| `readonly`) |
| `--gate <GATE>` | Target a specific parked approval gate by step id — required once a run has more than one gate parked at once (a concurrent DAG run with several gates in the same batch-park wave). Omit for the legacy/single-gate case: the sole parked gate is approved exactly as before. Approving one gate of several leaves the others parked; the run stays `awaiting_approval` until every gate is resolved |

<a id="rupu-workflow-reject"></a>
### `rupu workflow reject`

Reject a paused run. Marks it `rejected`; no further steps dispatch

```
rupu workflow reject [OPTIONS] <RUN_ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<RUN_ID>` | Full run id (`run_<ULID>`) of the run awaiting approval |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--reason <REASON>` | Optional human-readable reason recorded in the run's `error_message` |
| `--gate <GATE>` | Target a specific parked approval gate by step id — same targeting rule as `approve --gate`. Rejecting one gate of several runs THAT gate's `on_reject` cleanup chain and leaves the others parked; the run flips to `rejected` only once every gate is resolved |

<a id="rupu-workflow-cancel"></a>
### `rupu workflow cancel`

Cancel a running workflow run

```
rupu workflow cancel [OPTIONS] <RUN_ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<RUN_ID>` | Full run id (`run_<ULID>`) as printed by `rupu workflow run` |

<a id="rupu-workflow-pause"></a>
### `rupu workflow pause`

Cooperatively pause a running workflow run at its next safe boundary, leaving it non-terminal and resumable via `rupu workflow resume`

```
rupu workflow pause [OPTIONS] <RUN_ID>
```

|---|---|
| `<RUN_ID>` | Full run id (`run_<ULID>`) as printed by `rupu workflow run` |

<a id="rupu-workflow-resume"></a>
### `rupu workflow resume`

Resume a failed/cancelled run, re-running only the agent runs that didn't succeed. An agent run the interrupted process left mid-flight is picked up where it stopped (or its finished answer reused) rather than started over

```
rupu workflow resume [OPTIONS] <RUN_ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<RUN_ID>` | Full run id (`run_<ULID>`) of the terminal run to resume |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--mode <MODE>` | Override permission mode for the resumed run (`ask` \| `bypass` \| `readonly`) |
| `--plain` | Use the plain line printer instead of the live graph view |
| `--restart-interrupted` | Start every interrupted step and `for_each` unit over from its prompt instead of continuing it from its transcript |

<a id="rupu-agentiflow"></a>
### `rupu agentiflow`

Run goal-directed agent fleets (agentiflows)

```
rupu agentiflow [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Description |
|---|---|
| [`run`](#rupu-agentiflow-run) | Run an agentiflow in the foreground until its envelope stops it |
| [`list`](#rupu-agentiflow-list) | List agentiflow runs, newest first |
| [`status`](#rupu-agentiflow-status) | Show one agentiflow run: goals, budget, rounds and why it stopped |
| [`send`](#rupu-agentiflow-send) | Send a steering message to a running agentiflow's lead |
| [`stop`](#rupu-agentiflow-stop) | Stop a running agentiflow |
| [`attach`](#rupu-agentiflow-attach) | Watch an agentiflow run: its event log and its lead's current round |
| [`serve`](#rupu-agentiflow-serve) | Supervise agentiflow runs: reap the ones whose coordinator died |

<a id="rupu-agentiflow-run"></a>
### `rupu agentiflow run`

Run an agentiflow in the foreground until its envelope stops it. Loads `<project>/.rupu/agentiflows/<DEF>.yaml` (else `~/.rupu/agentiflows/<DEF>.yaml`), validates it against its engagement profiles, and runs it to a stop: goals met, coverage reached, a budget or ceiling, or an operator stop. Prints the run id up front (stderr) and the outcome at the end. With `--detach` the run goes to a background process of its own and the command returns as soon as the run has started, printing the run id on stdout; follow it with `agentiflow status <id>`, steer it with `send`, end it with `stop`. A run that cannot start (no credential, an invalid definition) is reported here with the cause, not left to fail unseen.

```
rupu agentiflow run [OPTIONS] <DEF>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<DEF>` | Agentiflow name (matches an `agentiflows/<name>.yaml` file) |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--detach` | Run in the background: start the run in its own process group and return once it has started. The background process's stderr is kept in `<run dir>/detach.log`; a run that fails before it starts has that error printed here and no run directory left behind |

<a id="rupu-agentiflow-list"></a>
### `rupu agentiflow list`

List agentiflow runs, newest first. Reads `<RUPU_HOME>/agentiflows/af_*/agentiflow.json`. The definition files that sit beside the run directories are not runs and are not listed (see `rupu agent list` / `rupu workflow list` for definitions).

```
rupu agentiflow list [OPTIONS]
```

<a id="rupu-agentiflow-status"></a>
### `rupu agentiflow status`

Show one agentiflow run: goals, budget, rounds and why it stopped

```
rupu agentiflow status [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<ID>` | Run id (`af_...`): the full id, the compact form `list` prints, or a unique prefix / suffix of it |

<a id="rupu-agentiflow-send"></a>
### `rupu agentiflow send`

Send a steering message to a running agentiflow's lead. The message is queued under the run's `steering/` directory and the envelope hands it to the lead at the next round boundary. `--now` marks it as an interrupt (for delivery mid-round); until the envelope acts on that mark, it is still delivered at the round boundary. A run that already finished takes no message.

```
rupu agentiflow send [OPTIONS] <ID> <MESSAGE>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<ID>` | Run id (`af_...`): the full id, the compact form `list` prints, or a unique prefix / suffix of it |
| `<MESSAGE>` | What to tell the lead |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--now` | Mark the message as an interrupt (mid-round delivery). Delivered at the round boundary until the envelope acts on the mark |

<a id="rupu-agentiflow-stop"></a>
### `rupu agentiflow stop`

Stop a running agentiflow. By default the stop is graceful: it is queued like a steering message, and the envelope winds the run down at the next round boundary (the units it launched are stopped with it). `--now` is the hard stop: it SIGTERMs the coordinator (and, for a detached run, the process group it leads, so what its lead's tools started goes too), SIGTERMs every unit still running (SIGKILL for one that outlives a short grace), then records the run as failed (`operator_stop:now`) without waiting for the round.

```
rupu agentiflow stop [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<ID>` | Run id (`af_...`): the full id, the compact form `list` prints, or a unique prefix / suffix of it |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--now` | Hard stop: signal the coordinator and its units now |

<a id="rupu-agentiflow-attach"></a>
### `rupu agentiflow attach`

Watch an agentiflow run: its event log and its lead's current round. Prints the run's `events.jsonl` (everything so far, then each line as it lands) and the lead's transcript for the round in progress, moving on to the next round's transcript as it starts. By default it follows the run until it ends (a goal met, a budget, a stop, a failure) and then prints why it stopped. `--no-follow` (`--once`) prints what the run has recorded so far and returns. Attaching to a run that already finished shows its log and returns at once. Ctrl-C leaves the run going.

```
rupu agentiflow attach [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<ID>` | Run id (`af_...`): the full id, the compact form `list` prints, or a unique prefix / suffix of it |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--no-follow` | Print what the run has recorded so far and return, instead of following it until it ends [aliases: --once] |

<a id="rupu-agentiflow-serve"></a>
### `rupu agentiflow serve`

Supervise agentiflow runs: reap the ones whose coordinator died. A coordinator that is killed (SIGKILL, a crash, the machine going down) leaves its run `running` forever and its detached units burning tokens. This runs a sweep at startup and then every `[agentiflow] serve_interval_secs` (default 60), recording each such run as failed (`orphaned: coordinator pid <p> not running`) and stopping its units. It runs until SIGTERM / Ctrl-C. `rupu cp serve` runs the same sweep on its own tick, so this is for hosts that do not run the control plane. `[agentiflow] serve_enabled = false` or `reaper_enabled = false` turns it off.

```
rupu agentiflow serve [OPTIONS]
```

| `--kind <KIND>` | Vendor this account authenticates against (anthropic \| openai \| gemini \| copilot \| github \| gitlab \| linear \| jira \| local). Required the first time an account name is used; inferred from config or from the account name afterwards |

<a id="rupu-auth-logout"></a>

Remove a stored credential

|---|---|

| `--mode <MODE>` | Specific auth mode to remove. If omitted, both api-key and sso for that provider are removed [possible values: api-key, sso] |
| `--all` | Remove every stored credential across all providers and modes |
| `--yes` | Skip the confirmation prompt for --all |

<a id="rupu-auth-backend"></a>

Show where credentials are stored. There is one backend: a chmod-600 JSON file at `~/.rupu/auth.json`. The OS keychain backend was retired.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--use <KIND>` | `file` — the only supported value, and already in effect. Accepted so existing scripts keep working; `keychain` is refused with an explanation. Omit to print where credentials currently live |
| `--view <VIEW>` | Human snapshot density (`focused` \| `compact` \| `full`) [default: full] [possible values: focused, compact, full] |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |
| `--pager` | Force pager. Default: page when stdout is a tty |
| `--no-pager` | Disable pager |

```
rupu netflow [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Description |

Print one run's netflow flow records


<a id="rupu-netflow-prune"></a>
### `rupu netflow prune`

Delete per-run netflow ledgers older than a cutoff

```
rupu netflow prune [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--older-than <DURATION>` | Retention cutoff, e.g. `30d`, `12h`, or `1w`. Must be positive — `0s` or a negative value is rejected, not treated as "everything". Defaults to `30d` (mirrors `transcript prune`'s own fallback) when omitted. A ledger is matched by file mtime, but a ledger whose run is still live is never deleted however old it is: a workflow run that is not finished (and whose recorded runner pid, if any, is alive) protects its own, its steps', its fan-out units' and its sub-agents' ledgers, and a standalone `rupu run` whose process is alive protects its own and its sub-agents'. Such ledgers are listed as `skipped_live`. Anything modified in roughly the last hour is never eligible regardless of what you pass here |
| `--dry-run` | Preview deletions without removing files. Always cheap to run first — the default (no flag) deletes immediately, same as `transcript prune` |

<a id="rupu-scm-bind"></a>
### `rupu scm bind`

Add an account-selection rule: route repos under an owner glob, or checkouts under a path glob, to a named account

```
rupu scm bind [OPTIONS] --account <ACCOUNT> <--owner <OWNER>|--path <PATH>>
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--owner <OWNER>` | Owner glob this rule matches (e.g. `acme/*` or `acme`). Matched against `RepoRef.owner` — the tier that works for daemons, which know the owner but have no cwd. Mutually exclusive with `--path`; exactly one is required |
| `--path <PATH>` | Filesystem-path glob this rule matches against the caller's cwd (e.g. `~/Code/work/*`). Mutually exclusive with `--owner` |
| `--account <ACCOUNT>` | The account this rule selects |

<a id="rupu-session-start"></a>
### `rupu session start`

Start a persistent agent session

```
rupu session start [OPTIONS] <AGENT> [TARGET] [PROMPT]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<AGENT>` | Agent name (matches an `agents/*.md` file) |
| `[TARGET]` | Optional target reference, e.g. `github:owner/repo#42` |
| `[PROMPT]` | Optional initial user message. Defaults to `go` if omitted |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--prompt <PROMPT_FLAG>` | Initial user message via flag (preferred over the positional `prompt`; lets a caller pass a prompt without it being parsed as a target) |
| `--mode <MODE>` | Override permission mode (`ask` \| `bypass` \| `readonly`) |
| `--no-stream` | Don't render tokens as they arrive, for every turn in this session. The request still streams on the wire, so long responses can't hit the request timeout |
| `--into <PATH>` | For repo targets: clone into this directory instead of `./<repo>/` |
| `--detach` | Start the first turn without auto-attaching |
| `--view <VIEW>` | Live renderer mode when auto-attaching [possible values: focused, compact, full] |
| `--engagement-profile <ID>` | Engagement profile(s) every turn of the session runs under — the asset domain(s) findings are validated against (e.g. `network`, `binary`). Repeatable or comma-separated. Empty = the `code` path [aliases: --engagement-profiles] |

<a id="rupu-issues-run"></a>
### `rupu issues run`

Convenience: run a workflow with an issue run-target. Equivalent to `rupu workflow run <name> <issue-ref>` (the run-target is a positional on `workflow run`, not a flag)

```
rupu issues run [OPTIONS] <WORKFLOW> <REF>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<WORKFLOW>` | Workflow filename stem under `.rupu/workflows/` (or `<global>/workflows/`). Same name `rupu workflow run` accepts |
| `<REF>` | Issue ref. Same shorthand rules as `show` |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--mode <MODE>` | Override permission mode (`ask` \| `bypass` \| `readonly`) |

<a id="rupu-mcp-serve"></a>
### `rupu mcp serve`

Run the MCP server for an external MCP-aware client

```
rupu mcp serve [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--transport <TRANSPORT>` | Transport. v0 ships stdio only; http returns NotWiredInV0 [default: stdio] [possible values: stdio, http] |
| `--tools <TOOLS>` | The tools to serve, in the agent `tools:` grammar: exact names, legacy aliases, `ns.*`, `core.*` or `*` (comma-separated or repeated). Default: the connector and findings tools (`scm.*,issues.*,github.*,gitlab.*,findings.*`) |
| `--mode <MODE>` | Permission mode each call is decided under: `bypass` (default — the MCP client's own confirmation UX is in front of every call), `readonly` (refuse workspace writes and external actions) or `ask` (no operator to prompt here, so it allows) [default: bypass] |

<a id="rupu-findings-export"></a>
### `rupu findings export`

Export findings as a report: one finding, or a project report. A single `--id` with no other selection writes that finding as a stand-alone document; anything else writes one report over the selection, or with `--split` a zip holding an index and one file per finding. Findings are numbered within their project (`SEC-001`, …) before the selection is applied, so a finding keeps its number whatever else is left out. The number prefix is `[findings].export_id_prefix` in the GLOBAL config (`~/.rupu/config.toml`); a project's `.rupu/config.toml` never changes it.

```
rupu findings export [OPTIONS] --output <PATH>
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--id <FINDING_ID>` | Export this finding (repeatable) |
| `--project <WS_ID|PATH>` | Only this project: a workspace id, or the path of its checkout |
| `--run <RUN_ID>` | Only the findings a run (and its sub-runs) declared |
| `--severity <SEVERITY>` | Only this severity and worse [possible values: critical, high, medium, low, info] |
| `--owner <OWNER>` | Only findings whose report names this owner |
| `--cwe <CWE-N>` | Only findings for this CWE (e.g. CWE-79), compared by number: CWE-79 never selects CWE-798 |
| `--include-summaries` | Keep findings recorded without a full report (left out by default) |
| `--split` | Write a zip of one file per finding plus an index |
| `--title <TITLE>` | Title of the project report (default: "Findings report") |
| `--to <TO>` | Document format [default: md] [possible values: md, html, pdf] |
| `-o, --output <PATH>` | Where to write the report. An existing directory receives the generated file name |

<a id="rupu-findings-import"></a>
### `rupu findings import`

Attach reports written before the full profile to their findings. A one-time migration aid: reads Markdown finding reports in the report layout, and attaches each to the summary finding its `Finding ID:` line names (also read: `Native Finding:`, `Rupu Finding ID:` and similar labels; an id mentioned only in prose is never used). The finding becomes a full-profile finding. A report attaches whole or not at all; a finding that already has a report is left alone; each changed ledger is backed up first (`findings.jsonl.pre-import-<time>`).

```
rupu findings import [OPTIONS] <PATH>...
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<PATH>...` | Report files, or directories to search for `*.md` files |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--id <FINDING_ID>` | The finding a single report belongs to, for a report with no `Finding ID:` line. Only with one file; refused when the report's own `Finding ID:` line names a different finding |
| `--dry-run` | Parse and validate every report, check that the artifacts it lists exist and that it is within the size limits once they are recorded; write nothing (no ledger change, backup or lock file). No artifact is copied (only its first 8 KiB is read), so trouble found only while copying one shows up only on a real import |

<a id="rupu-findings-list"></a>
### `rupu findings list`

List findings matching a query, e.g. `severity>=high -tag:noise`. Put flags (`--ids-only`, `--limit`) before the query words.

```
rupu findings list [OPTIONS] [QUERY]...
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `[QUERY]...` | Findings query, e.g. `severity>=high tag:class:sqli -tag:false-positive`. Several words are joined with spaces; quote anything with `>`, `<` or spaces for your shell. Keys: severity (>=,>,<=,<), tag, has, project, cwe, owner, product, verified, profile, scope, concern, agent, workflow, file, run, id; bare words search title/summary/id/file. Put flags before the query words |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--limit <N>` | Show at most N findings; how many were left out goes to stderr |
| `--ids-only` | Print only the finding ids, one per line |

<a id="rupu-findings-tag"></a>
### `rupu findings tag`

Add or remove tags on findings. Tags are free-form: lowercase a-z, 0-9 and `. _ : / -`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 characters (`Needs-POC` is stored as `needs-poc`). Give `-` as the only id to read ids from stdin, one per line: `rupu findings list --ids-only tag:class:sqli | rupu findings tag - --add needs-poc`. Findings in different projects are changed project by project; an unknown id fails the command after the rest are changed.

```
rupu findings tag [OPTIONS] <FINDING_ID>...
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<FINDING_ID>...` | Finding ids, or `-` alone to read them from stdin |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--add <TAG>` | Tag to add (repeatable) |
| `--remove <TAG>` | Tag to remove (repeatable) |

<a id="rupu-findings-tags"></a>
### `rupu findings tags`

List the tags in use, with how many findings carry each (optionally only on the findings a query selects)

```
rupu findings tags [OPTIONS] [QUERY]...
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `[QUERY]...` | Count only the tags on findings this query selects (same syntax as `findings list`) |

<a id="rupu-cron-list"></a>

<a id="rupu-cron-tick"></a>
### `rupu cron tick`

Walk all workflows, fire any whose schedule matches between the persisted `last_fired` and now. Designed to run from system cron at 1-minute granularity

```
rupu cron tick [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Don't actually run workflows or update state; just print what would fire. Useful for verifying a `crontab` line |
| `--skip-events` | Run only the cron-scheduled tier; skip event polling. Useful for crontab lines that want predictable cost |
| `--only-events` | Run only the event-polling tier; skip cron-scheduled fires. Useful for splitting tick frequencies (cron at 1 min, events at 5 min) |


|---|---|
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |

<a id="rupu-cp-serve"></a>
### `rupu cp serve`

Start the control-plane HTTP server. Also runs three in-process background loops on a timer, not just the HTTP server: the autoflow reconciler, the cron/event-trigger tick, and the gate sweep (enforces gate `on_timeout` routing and reaps orphaned runs with a dead `runner_pid`). Each loop is gated by a `[cp]` config key and defaults to enabled at a 60s interval: `autoflow_reconcile_enabled`, `cron_tick_enabled`, `gate_sweep_enabled` (see `rupu-config`'s `CpConfig`). Exits non-zero immediately if the bind address is already taken; when the occupant is another rupu control plane, the error names its PID.

```
rupu cp serve [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--bind <BIND>` | Address to bind. Defaults to 127.0.0.1:7878 [default: 127.0.0.1:7878] |
| `--token <TOKEN>` | Optional access token. If set, every `/api/*` call needs it, as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or the browser's token cookie. The printed (and auto-opened) URL carries `?token=<token>`; opening it signs that browser in (cookie set, token dropped from the URL). `/healthz` and the page shell stay open; the UI shows no data until the browser is signed in |
| `--no-open` | Do not open the served URL in a browser on startup. By default the URL is opened when running interactively (a terminal); the URL is always printed regardless |

<a id="rupu-host-add"></a>
### `rupu host add`

Register a remote rupu-cp host

```
rupu host add [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` | Display name for the host |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--url <URL>` | Base URL of the remote rupu-cp instance (e.g. https://rupu.example.com). Mutually exclusive with `--ssh` and `--bucket` |
| `--ssh <SSH>` | SSH destination: `user@host` or an `~/.ssh/config` alias. Selects the Ssh transport. Mutually exclusive with `--url` and `--bucket` |
| `--port <PORT>` | SSH port override (default: 22). Only relevant with `--ssh` |
| `--identity <IDENTITY>` | Path to an SSH identity file. Only relevant with `--ssh` |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` | Object-store URL for the bucket transport (`s3://…` / `gs://…` / `file://…`). Selects the Bucket transport. Mutually exclusive with `--url` and `--ssh`. Credentials come from the environment / cloud credential chain and are never stored |
| `--prefix <PREFIX>` | Object-store key prefix (optional). Only relevant with `--bucket` |
| `--token <TOKEN>` | API token. Mutually exclusive with `--token-stdin`. Only relevant with `--url` |
| `--token-stdin` | Read the API token from stdin (one line). Mutually exclusive with `--token` |

| Subcommand | Description |
|---|---|
| [`enroll`](#rupu-node-enroll) | Enroll a new tunnel node in the local host store and print the `rupu node --cp-url ... --token ...` command to run on the box.  The token is shown ONCE and never persisted on disk |
| [`pull`](#rupu-node-pull) | Poll a bucket dead-drop, atomically claim jobs, run them locally, write results back, and apply queued control messages |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--cp-url <CP_URL>` | WebSocket URL of the control-plane node endpoint (e.g. `ws://cp.example.com:7878/api/node/connect`; the `/api/node/connect` path is appended automatically when omitted). `wss://` requires a TLS-terminating proxy and a TLS-enabled build. Required in agent mode (when no subcommand is given) |
| `--token <TOKEN>` | Authentication token.  Mutually exclusive with `--token-stdin` |
| `--token-stdin` | Read the authentication token from stdin (one line). Preferred over `--token` so the secret does not land in shell history.  Mutually exclusive with `--token` |
| `--node-id <NODE_ID>` | Override the node identity string.  Default: a persistent `node_<ULID>` written to `~/.rupu/node_id` on first run |

<a id="rupu-node-enroll"></a>
### `rupu node enroll`

Enroll a new tunnel node in the local host store and print the `rupu node --cp-url ... --token ...` command to run on the box.  The token is shown ONCE and never persisted on disk

```
rupu node enroll [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` | Display name for the node (e.g. `build-box-01`) |

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--cp-url <CP_URL>` | CP URL to include in the printed command (e.g. `ws://cp.example.com:7878`; the `/api/node/connect` path is appended automatically when omitted).  Default: this machine's detected routable IP on port 7878 |

<a id="rupu-node-pull"></a>
### `rupu node pull`

Poll a bucket dead-drop, atomically claim jobs, run them locally, write results back, and apply queued control messages

```
rupu node pull [OPTIONS] --bucket <BUCKET>
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` | Bucket URL (e.g. `s3://my-bucket`, `gs://my-bucket`). Credentials are resolved via the environment credential chain |
| `--prefix <PREFIX>` | Optional key prefix within the bucket (e.g. `rupu/host-1`) |
| `--host-id <HOST_ID>` | Override the worker identity.  Default: the stable `node_<ULID>` persisted at `~/.rupu/node_id` (same as the tunnel node agent) |
| `--once` | Claim all currently-available jobs, drain them to terminal (bounded), then exit.  In loop mode (the default) the agent runs forever |
| `--interval <INTERVAL>` | Poll interval between ticks in seconds (loop mode only) [default: 15] |

<a id="rupu-update"></a>
### `rupu update`

Download and install the latest release for the configured channel

```
rupu update [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--check` | Only report whether an update is available; install nothing |
| `--force` | Reinstall even if already up to date (or downgrade to the channel's latest if this build is ahead of it) |
| `-y, --yes` | Deprecated no-op: `rupu update` no longer prompts, so there is nothing to skip. Still accepted so existing scripts and aliases that pass `-y` keep working |
| `--channel <beta|stable>` | Override the configured channel for this run |
| `--rollback` | Restore the previously-installed binary from the last backup |
| `--print-platform` | Print this build's release-asset platform name (e.g. `linux-x64`) and exit. The release pipeline uses this to name assets from the binary itself, so the publisher and `rupu update` cannot drift |
